_meta.editorial_context: Plate-4 of /fiscal/ shows what the government itself commits to — the trajectory under DoF's own definition of operating vs capital. Read alongside plate-5 (PBO reclassification) the reader sees both views: DoF's stated operating balance reaches +$0.9bn in 2028-29; PBO's reclassified view has the operating deficit still at $18.1bn that year (using stricter IMF GFS 2014 capital definition).

_meta.headline_finding: Under DoF's own definition (SEU 2026), the day-to-day operating balance crosses zero in FY2028-29 (+$0.9bn), exactly the year the fiscal anchor commits to. The track climbs from a -$26.4bn deficit in FY2025-26 to a +$6.1bn surplus by FY2030-31 — improvement of $32.5bn over six years. The plate-5 PBO reclassification is the counterpoint: even under DoF's friendly capital definition, the path is real; the policy debate is whether DoF's capital definition is too generous (PBO says yes, by $94bn over six years).
